```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(factoextra)

lithics_clean <- read_csv("lithics_clean.csv")

```

```{r}
# prepare the data for PCA
pca_data <- 
  lithics_clean |> 
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  drop_na()

# compute PCA
pca_result <-
  prcomp(pca_data, scale. = TRUE)


```

```{r}
#| label: fig-kmeans-silhouette
#| fig-cap: "Choosing the number of clusters for k-means"

# silhouette plot to choose the number of clusters
silhouette_plot <-
  fviz_nbclust(pca_result$x, kmeans, method = "silhouette", k.max = 10) +
  labs(title = "k-means plot")

silhouette_plot

# the best k is the one with the highest average silhouette width
best_k <-
  silhouette_plot$data |>
  slice_max(y, n = 1) |>
  pull(clusters) |>
  as.integer()

# run k-means on the PCA scores
set.seed(459)

kmeans_result <-
  kmeans(pca_result$x, centers = best_k, nstart = 25)

# cluster labels for the biplot
cluster <- factor(kmeans_result$cluster)

```

@fig-kmeans-silhouette shows the clusters based on the widths of the artefacts. In the PCA plot we can see that the lower period lithics are smaller in length, width, and thickness, the middle period lithics are thicker and wider, but have varied lenghts, and the upper period lithics are smaller in lenght, but have varied thickness and width. In the k-means plot we see the clusters based on the differing widths of the lithics shown.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-biplot
#| fig-cap: "lab 3"

fviz_pca(pca_result,
         geom.ind = "point",
         habillage = cluster,
         palette = "Dark2",
         repel = TRUE,
         title = "")
          
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-contr
#| fig-cap: "homework"

# how much each PC is telling us
fviz_eig(pca_result,
         choice = "eigenvalue",
         parallel = TRUE,
         title = "")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-contri-original
#| fig-cap: "homework"

fviz_contrib(pca_result,
             choice = "var",
             axes = 1)

```
